principle_text: When the persuadee redirects the conversation to the social issue, avoid sharing personal information that does not clearly connect to the donation goal or charity.
When the persuadee shows curiosity or openness, you should connect a personal, relatable story to the cause to create emotional engagement and increase their interest in supporting the charity.
When a persuadee shares personal information or sensitive topics, avoid making jokes or insensitive remarks that could cause discomfort or offense.
When the persuadee expresses personal hardship or need, avoid referencing external political events that may seem insensitive or irrelevant to their current situation.
When the persuadee shows curiosity about personal details unrelated to the charitable cause, avoid sharing information that does not connect back to the donation goal or charity mission.
When the persuadee shares personal information unrelated to the charity, avoid responding with equally unrelated personal details that do not guide the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee shows only basic awareness of a charity after personal rapport, avoid assuming strong interest without further engagement or evidence of commitment.
When the persuadee shows familiarity with the charity, you should make a clear, specific donation request to encourage immediate commitment.
When the persuadee expresses ambivalence or neutrality about children, avoid asking personal questions that do not connect to the charitable cause or donation goal.
When the persuadee expresses concern for a broad group beyond the specific focus, avoid narrowing the issue too quickly without acknowledging their wider perspective.
When the persuadee responds with neutral interest in personal details, avoid sharing unrelated personal information that does not guide the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee shares personal family details, avoid responding with unrelated personal information that does not connect to the donation goal or encourage commitment.
When the persuadee shows personal engagement and openness, you should smoothly transition from personal topics to introducing the charity to pique their curiosity and interest.
When the persuadee shows interest or affinity for a cause, you should provide a clear, concise explanation of the charity’s mission that connects emotionally and highlights urgent needs.
When the persuadee expresses interest or positive feelings related to the cause, you should ask questions that highlight their values to build rapport and align them with the charitable mission.
When the persuadee expresses positive feelings toward the cause, you should directly invite them to consider helping to increase engagement and willingness to donate.
When the persuadee expresses willingness to help vulnerable groups, you should directly connect your request to their desire to assist, reinforcing their engagement and openness to support.
When the persuadee expresses willingness to help a cause, you should ask specific, relatable questions that connect their willingness to concrete actions or needs.
When the persuadee expresses hesitation or seeks clarification about the charity, avoid asking about donation amounts prematurely before establishing trust and clear information.
When the persuadee shares personal information unrelated to donation intent, avoid focusing solely on agreement and personal questions that do not advance the donation conversation.

When the persuadee shows empathy for vulnerable children and supports related organizations, you should present specific, impactful statistics to deepen their emotional engagement and motivate charitable support.

When the persuadee expresses empathy or sadness about the plight of those in need, you should acknowledge and build on these emotions to deepen their emotional engagement and increase willingness to donate.
When the persuadee shows openness to continue the conversation, avoid only polite engagement without steering towards the donation goal or increasing donation willingness.
When the persuadee expresses personal concern for loved ones, you should evoke empathy by asking them to imagine a distressing situation involving those loved ones to increase emotional engagement.
When the persuadee expresses empathy and concern for a problem, you should acknowledge their feelings and introduce actionable solutions to increase their engagement and willingness to help.
When the persuadee indicates no prior volunteering experience, avoid focusing solely on volunteering questions that do not directly connect to their willingness to donate or engage with the cause.
When the persuadee provides mild personal information without expressing interest or commitment, avoid asking questions that do not deepen engagement or connect to the donation goal.
When the persuadee indicates occasional charitable donations without strong commitment, avoid asking generic donation questions that do not encourage deeper engagement or commitment.
When the persuadee shows some openness to charitable causes, you should directly ask for a donation to encourage commitment and move closer to the donation goal.
When the persuadee shows uncertainty about a charity, you should introduce the charity with a question to engage their curiosity and invite further conversation.
When the persuadee expresses mixed feelings about a topic related to the charity, avoid assuming uniform positive emotions or pushing only positive associations.
When the persuadee expresses mixed feelings about family, you should evoke shared values and commitment to wellbeing to build rapport and encourage agreement.
When the persuadee expresses shared values and agreement, you should introduce the charitable cause naturally to build curiosity and increase engagement.
When the persuadee expresses sympathy and willingness to help, you should ask questions that evoke their emotions and reinforce their positive feelings toward the cause.
When the persuadee introduces a topic related to charitable giving, avoid merely agreeing without advancing the conversation toward a donation request.
